memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'It is just as I said to Pharaoh: God has shown Pharaoh what he is about to do. Seven years of great abundance are coming throughout the land of Egypt, but seven years of famine will follow them. Then all the abundance in Egypt will be forgotten, and the famine will ravage the land. The abundance in the land will not be remembered, because the famine that follows it will be so severe. The reason the dream was given to Pharaoh in two forms is that the matter has been firmly decided by God, and God will do it soon.'" - Gen 41:28-32 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Joseph presses the point home: this is no vague possibility. "The matter has been firmly decided by God, and God will do it soon." The reason Pharaoh dreamed it twice, in two different forms, was to underline its certainty. What God had shown would surely come to pass. The abundance and the famine were not "maybes" — they were settled in the sovereign plan of God.

Here we meet the reassuring, and sometimes sobering, truth of God's sovereignty. God rules over the harvests and the famines, the years of plenty and the years of want. History is not a series of random accidents; it unfolds according to the purposes of a God who reigns over all. What He has decided will come to be.

For God's people, this is a deep comfort. The events of our lives and our world are not spinning out of control. Behind the headlines, behind the good years and the hard years, is a God who reigns. "Our God is in heaven; he does whatever pleases him" (Ps 115:3). We can face an uncertain future because it rests in the hands of a certain God.

At the same time, God's sovereignty calls for our response. Because God had decided, Pharaoh needed to prepare. God's settled plans do not make our actions pointless; they call us to align with what He is doing. Trust the God who reigns over history, and then live wisely in light of what He has shown.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I trust that God reigns over history and my future?
2. How does God's sovereignty comfort me about an uncertain world?
3. How should God's settled purposes shape the way I live?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You reign over all things, and what You decide surely comes to pass. Help me to rest in Your sovereignty over my uncertain world, and to live wisely in light of what You have shown. Amen.
